browser: Native macOS Safari 27, controlled through the application UI and Web Inspector

helpBeforeFix.visibleChecks: Paused court, Menu, Help open/close rendered on both origins

parkedContextBefore.mechanism: Switch to 2D; induce real WEBGL_lose_context on retained renderer; wait for contextlost; reopen 3D
parkedContextBefore.visual: Court and athletes absent; target and application controls still visible

parkedContextAfter.diagnosticWarning: Three.js disposal attempted forceContextLoss on an already lost context; its extension was then unavailable

helpAfterRecovery.visual: Rendered court, athletes, ball and target inspected after recovery and all repeated Help transitions

limits: The historical Help-only blank observation has not been causally connected to parked context loss. Its spontaneous cause is not claimed resolved by this evidence alone.
Controlled probes are distinct from visible-interface journeys; they use application methods and the real WebGL loss extension.
Native screenshots were inspected in the tool transcript; no personal browser windows, clipboard content or account data were stored in repository evidence.

The first local probe import failed because .mjs was served as application/octet-stream. The probe was renamed .js, and subsequent imports executed. This was a QA helper MIME issue, not a product error.
Some native UI actions returned before the accessibility state settled. A later observation established console execution; no Safari settings or security permissions were changed.
